text:
ItemKNN starts with deduplicated binary training incidence X[user,item], support d_i=Σ_u X_ui, and co-occurrence C=XᵀX. Cosine S_ij=C_ij/√(d_i d_j); remove the diagonal before selecting neighbors. Normalize similarities before top-K: pruning raw counts first can discard genuine cosine neighbors. Optional row normalization after pruning rescales retained edges but cannot recover discarded neighbors; pruning also generally breaks symmetry. Specify whether K applies per source row or target column. [RecBole implementation](https://recbole.io/docs/_modules/recbole/model/general_recommender/itemknn.html). Popularity correction is established: GRU4Rec’s baseline uses C_ij/[(d_i+λ)^α(d_j+λ)^(1−α)], with α=0.5 giving regularized cosine and λ discounting rare-item coincidences. [Reference code](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec/blob/master/baselines.py).

Session-kNN instead retrieves neighboring sessions using binary-set overlap, then sums neighbor similarities over sessions containing each candidate; it need not construct an item graph. Vanilla overlap ignores order; STAN adds position and time weighting. [Session-kNN code](https://github.com/rn5l/session-rec/blob/master/algorithms/knn/sknn.py), [STAN paper](https://doi.org/10.1145/3331184.3331322). Directed transitions count chronological i→j events within each training history: adjacent pairs give first-order counts; sequential rules extend to bounded gaps with weights such as 1/gap. [Sequential-rules implementation](https://github.com/rn5l/session-rec/blob/master/algorithms/baselines/sr.py). A reproducible Markov variant row-normalizes counts. Normalizing before pruning preserves retained probabilities; renormalizing afterward conditions on retained destinations. Self-transition removal is an explicit choice, unlike suppressing trivial cosine self-neighbors.

Scalable recipe: per category, compute sparse blocks X[:,block]ᵀX, normalize nonzeros, clear self-edges, retain row top-K, and append CSR output; bound block size because sparse products can become dense. Alternatively normalize item vectors first and use fused sparse multiplication/top-K, requesting K+1 before self-removal. [sparse_dot_topn](https://github.com/ing-bank/sparse_dot_topn). Assessment: adding these scores to SASRec is a neighborhood/transition ensemble; novelty requires evidence beyond the established graph construction.
